name: Malva pudding
summary: A soft, spongy apricot-jam pudding baked until caramel-brown, then soaked in a hot butter and cream sauce and served warm with custard.
about: Malva pudding is a South African baked pudding whose exact origin is uncertain; the name is often linked to Malvasia (Madeira) wine. Spongy, caramelised and soaked in a buttery cream sauce, it became the country's favourite winter dessert, served at Sunday lunches, church bazaars and restaurants.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C for a fan oven). Grease a 2-litre ovenproof dish (about 20 × 30 cm) with butter.
Beat the soft butter, sugar and egg together with an electric beater for 3–4 minutes, until pale and thick. Beat in the apricot jam.
Stir the vinegar and vanilla into the milk. Sift the flour, bicarbonate of soda and salt into another bowl.
Fold the flour and the milk into the egg mixture in turns, a third at a time, until you have a smooth, runny batter with no dry pockets.
Pour the batter into the dish and bake for 40–45 minutes, until risen, deep caramel-brown on top and a skewer pushed into the centre comes out clean.

While it bakes, put the cream, butter, sugar and hot water in a saucepan over low heat and stir for 3–4 minutes, until the butter has melted and the sugar dissolved. Keep it hot but do not let it boil.
As soon as the pudding comes out of the oven, prick it all over with a skewer and pour the hot sauce slowly over it. Leave it for 10 minutes to soak up the sauce; it will look glossy and sticky.
Serve warm, with warm custard poured over each portion.
prepNote: Bake and sauce it a day ahead; cover and reheat at 160 °C for 15 minutes before serving.
